tier1: This enterprise API gateway has three vulnerability classes: a CORS misconfiguration that exposes an internal admin-key endpoint to any origin, an XXE vulnerability in the document import endpoint that can read local files (including appsettings.json), and a dangerous deserialization sink where the session cookie is processed with BinaryFormatter despite a comment claiming it uses XmlSerializer.
tier2: CORS bypass: GET /api/internal/admin-key from any origin returns an admin session token — use it as the marl_session cookie or X-Session-Token header, then GET /admin to read FLAG_LOCAL. XXE bypass: POST /api/documents/import with Content-Type: application/xml and a payload using <!DOCTYPE x [<!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM 'file:///app/appsettings.json'>]> — the XmlUrlResolver resolves the entity and returns the file contents in the response. RCE: the marl_session cookie is base64(BinaryFormatter.Serialize(UserSession)) — generate a BinaryFormatter gadget chain (e.g. TypeConfuseDelegate via ysoserial.net) and submit it as the cookie value; the server deserializes it on every authenticated request, executing your command to read /flag_proof.txt.
